documents.text: Rust ownership and borrowing let the compiler enforce memory safety without a garbage collector.
Java uses a garbage collector to reclaim unreachable objects automatically.
PostgreSQL uses MVCC so reads and writes can proceed concurrently inside transactions.
MySQL can accelerate keyword lookups with B-tree indexes and full-text search.
Vector databases store dense embeddings and use approximate nearest neighbor indexes for semantic search.
BM25 ranks documents for lexical search with token frequency and inverse document frequency.
Kubernetes Deployments manage rolling updates and keep a desired replica count.
Docker images are built from layered filesystem snapshots and shared base images.

documents.text: Rust ownership and borrowing prevent use-after-free bugs and provide memory safety without relying on a garbage collector.
Java's garbage collector automatically reclaims objects, but pauses and heap tuning can affect latency.
PostgreSQL implements MVCC so transactions can isolate reads and writes without blocking every reader.
MySQL InnoDB also uses MVCC for transactions, but operational behavior and defaults differ from PostgreSQL.
Approximate nearest neighbor indexes in vector databases are used to retrieve semantically similar embeddings quickly.
Hybrid search combines lexical ranking like BM25 with embedding similarity to improve retrieval quality.
Kubernetes Deployments coordinate rolling updates, replica availability, and rollback history for services.
Horizontal Pod Autoscalers change replica counts based on observed CPU or custom metrics.
